title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
label: Freddie Datsun

won.source: USPW Stars, Stripes and Slams, "Saturday, Week 4, 2007" (in-game; the show's header omits the month, and it follows Tuesday, Week 4, January 2007, after which the narrator has "a big event to book for this Saturday").

how: Won from Bruce the Giant at Stars, Stripes and Slams with the Patriot Press; kept against William Hayes in February and against Peter Valentine and Umaga (by disqualification) in March, with a stretcher exit in between. It ends on the third show of March 2007, when Umaga beats him in a steel cage match.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
label: Umaga

won.source: USPW All American Wrestling, Saturday, Week 3, March 2007 (in-game), billed "New USPW World Champion: Umaga".

how: Won from Freddie Datsun in a steel cage match on the third show of March 2007 with a Savage Charge; kept against Datsun, Trent Shaffer, Muffin and Datsun again through May, and still champion at the end of this range, with Triple D set to challenge at the first Family Night. On the fourth Saturday of May 2007 he beats Muffin again; in June 2007 he keeps it against Triple D at the first Family Night, Freddie Datsun on the Saturday of Week 2 and Triple D again on the fourth Family Night, and is still champion at the end of the diary's June 2007 posts. In July 2007 he keeps it against William Hayes at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 4; it ends at the Family Night of Friday, Week 1, August 2007, when Darryl Devine beats him in a steel cage match.

title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
label: Citizen X

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Wednesday, Week 2, January 2007 (in-game).

how: Won from Jim Force with a golf club on the second show of the diary; kept against Force twice, Frankie Perez, Captain USA and Bulldozer Brandon Smith, the last billed as the fifth defense. It ends on the third show of March 2007, when Steve Flash beats him with the Flash Bang.

title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
label: Steve Flash

won.source: USPW All American Wrestling, Saturday, Week 3, March 2007 (in-game), billed "NEW USPW National Champion: Steve Flash".

how: Won from Citizen X with the Flash Bang on the third show of March 2007; kept against Fumihiro Ota, Corporal Doom, William Hayes by disqualification, and Ota and Hayes together in the April shows, and still champion at the end of this range. It ends at the first Family Night, Friday of Week 1, June 2007, when William Hayes beats him in a two out of three falls match.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Dudez!!!1!

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Tuesday, Week 3, January 2007 (in-game).

how: Won from The Towers of Power by Trent Shaffer and Mainstream Hernandez, then lost a week later when Frankie Perez hit Hernandez with a boot.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Canadian Crusties

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Tuesday, Week 4, January 2007 (in-game).

how: Won from The Dudez!!!1! after Frankie Perez hit Mainstream Hernandez, then kept against the Lords of War on the first March show. It ends on the third show of March 2007, when The Dudez!!!1! win a three-way match with Maxmillion Productions.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Dudez!!!1!

won.source: USPW All American Wrestling, Saturday, Week 3, March 2007 (in-game), billed "NEW USPW World Tag Team Champions: The Dudez!!!1!!!".

how: Won in a three-way match with Maxmillion Productions from The Canadian Crusties, who were not showing up for work; kept against The Demons of Rage and Veteran Mentality in April, and still champions at the end of this range, with a defense against the Demons of Rage set for the diary's first Family Night. In June 2007 they keep the belts against The Demons of Rage at the first Family Night, Demon Anger's last match, and against Veteran Mentality at the fourth; after that match Trent Shaffer attacks the champions with a steel chair and carries the belts off, and on the Saturday that follows he wears them and claims to be the champion with a partner he does not name, but the diary records no match and no change of champions. In July 2007 Trent Shaffer's long-promised partner turns out to be Chance Fortune; the pair, billed as the dudes, challenge for the belts: The Dudez!!!1! beat them at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 3 and take the belts back, and beat them again on the Monday of Week 2, August 2007, and they are still champions at the end of this range. It ends at Summer of Love, Saturday of Week 3, August 2007, when Team Seduction beat them and win the belts.

title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
label: William Hayes

won.source: USPW Family Night, Friday, Week 1, June 2007 (in-game), billed "Winner and new Champion: William Hayes".

how: Won from Steve Flash in a two out of three falls match at the first Family Night, Friday of Week 1, June 2007, with the Slick Trick; kept in June against Art Reed, Freddie Datsun, Muffin and Wanda Fish, and still champion at the end of this range. In July 2007 he keeps it against Jacob Jett on the Monday of Week 3; the same week he wins the fatal four-way for the number one contendership, and he loses the World Championship match to Umaga on the Thursday of Week 4; in August he keeps the belt against Wanda Fish on the Monday of Week 2, and is still champion at the end of this range. In August 2007 he keeps the belt against Bulldozer Brandon Smith on the Monday of Week 3 and against Art Reed at the Family Night of Friday, Week 3; in September he keeps it against Rudy Velasquez on the Monday of Week 1, and he is still champion at the end of this range, with Wanda Fish set to challenge him at Blaze of Glory. It ends at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, when Triple D hits Wanda Fish with the belt in the ring and she wins the title by disqualification; Hayes is fired in October 2007.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
label: Team Seduction

won.source: USPW Summer of Love!, Saturday, Week 3, August 2007 (in-game), recapped "Team Seduction defeated The Dudez!!!1!!! to win the USPW World Tag Team titles".

how: Won from The Dudez!!!1! at Summer of Love, Saturday of Week 3, August 2007, when Human Arsenal pins Mainstream Hernandez with an Ammo Dump after Fumihiro Ota's Ninja Strike, with Seduction at ringside; The Dudez!!!1! use their rematch clause, which Seduction turns into a ladder match for Blaze of Glory, and Team Seduction are still champions at the end of this range. They keep the belts against The Dudez!!!1! in a ladder match at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, when Seduction distracts Frankie Perez and Human Arsenal pulls the belts down; Seduction names Veteran Mentality the #1 contenders on the Monday of Week 4, and Team Seduction are still champions at the end of this range. In October 2007 they beat Veteran Mentality (with Steve Flash on the Thursday of Week 1, with Wanda Fish on the Monday of Week 2) and keep the belts against Veteran Mentality at A Haunting in America, Saturday of Week 2, after attacking the pair before the match; Team Seduction are still champions at the end of this range. They lose the belts to The Valentines at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, when Triple D, shut out of Divinity's plans, hits Human Arsenal with a Divine Dream Drop and lays Peter Valentine across him for the pin.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
label: Darryl Devine

won.source: USPW Family Night, Friday, Week 1, August 2007 (in-game), billed "Winner and NEW Champion: Triple D".

how: Won from Umaga in a steel cage match at the Family Night of Friday, Week 1, August 2007, by dropping from the top of the cage to the floor while Umaga is still on the steel steps; still champion at the end of this range. He keeps it against Bruce the Giant at the Family Night of Friday, Week 2, August 2007, against William Hayes at Summer of Love, against Freddie Datsun at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 1, September and against Jim Force at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 2; he is still champion at the end of this range, with Muffin set to challenge him at Blaze of Glory. At Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, he beats Muffin in a match the narrator rates an A, after the referee counts her pin and Seduction tells him Devine's foot was on the rope, and Danny Jillefski has the match restarted; on the Monday of Week 4 he leaves her bloodied in a cage match, an angle with no result; he is still champion at the end of this range, set to defend against Sam Strong at A Haunting in America. In October 2007 he beats Frankie Perez on the Monday of Week 2 with the Hotshots' help, beats Bruce the Giant on the Thursday when Seduction counts the pin, and keeps the belt against Sam Strong, back from retirement, at A Haunting in America on Saturday of Week 2 by pulling the tights, then against Davey Wayne on the Monday of Week 3; on the Thursday of Week 3 Freddie Datsun wins the number one contendership and walks off with the belt in a brawl without the title changing hands, and Devine is still champion at the end of this range, set to defend against Datsun at Pilgrimage on 22 November 2007. In November 2007 he keeps the belt against Umaga on the Monday of Week 1, in a match the narrator rates an A*, after Danny Jillefski, Big Cat Brandon and a low blow turn it and while the Masked Man's video threatens Seduction and Muffin, and against Freddie Datsun at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November, when the Masked Man hits Datsun with the Slick Trick and Jillefski, in a referee's shirt, counts the pin; he is still champion at the end of this range. Through the Monday of Week 4, December 2007 no title match is booked: he beats Casey Valentine, Fumihiro Ota, Human Arsenal, Rick Law, Wolf Hawkins and Reaper in non-title and singles matches, learns that the Masked Man is Jack Giedroyc, and the card for Winter Epiphany lists Giedroyc against him for the World Championship; he is still champion at the end of this range.

title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
label: Wanda Fish

won.source: USPW Blaze of Glory, Saturday, Week 2, September 2007 (in-game), recapped "Wanda Fish defeated William Hayes by DQ to win the USPW National title".

how: Won from William Hayes at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, after Danny Jillefski changes the rules so that the title can change hands on a disqualification: with Hayes and Fish facing each other in the ring, Triple D takes the belt from the timekeeper, hits Fish in the head with it and drops it on her, and the timekeeper announces her as the new champion; Jacob Jett's offer that she join Divinity and the sneak attacks that follow do not take it from her, and she is still champion at the end of this range, with Jett set to challenge her at A Haunting in America. She keeps the belt against Jacob Jett at A Haunting in America on Saturday of Week 2, October 2007, with the Dish of the Day; she is still champion at the end of this range, with Jett and Art Reed booked into a three-way against her for Pilgrimage. She keeps the belt at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, pinning Art Reed with the Dish of the Day in the three-way with Reed and Jacob Jett, who fight each other; she is still champion at the end of this range. Jillefski books Phlex as her challenger for Winter Epiphany on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 1, December 2007, after she and Phlex become a couple; Giant Oak and The Flash warn her Phlex is using her, and she beats The Flash in 12:54 on the Thursday of Week 3; she is still champion at the end of this range.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
label: Bruce the Giant

won.source: The diary's first show (Wednesday, Week 1, January 2007) has him as champion; it does not date the win; dates are the diary's own in-game dates.

how: Bruce the Giant's reign as the diary opens; the diary does not say when he won it. He loses the belt to Freddie Datsun at Stars, Stripes and Slams.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Valentines

won.source: USPW Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007 (in-game), billed "USPW Tag Team Championship Match- The Valentines vs. Team Seduction (c)" and recapped "The Valentines defeated Team Seduction to win the USPW Tag Team titles".

how: Won from Team Seduction at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, when Triple D, shut out of Divinity's plans, slides into the ring while Seduction distracts the referee, hits Human Arsenal and then Peter Valentine with Divine Dream Drops and lays Valentine across Arsenal, and the referee counts the pin; Danny Jillefski, who cannot reverse the decision, gives them a match on the spot against Divinity's "newest members", The Hotshots, and they lose the belts to them in 1:56.

title: uspw-65-and-older-unappreciated-championship
label: Bulldozer Brandon Smith

won.source: USPW Blaze of Glory, Saturday, Week 2, September 2007 (in-game), billed "USPW Unappreciated Championship Match", "Winner: Bulldozer Brandon Smith in 9:08".

how: Won in the four-way at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007: he promises Thomas Morgan his back, drops him with a Backdrop Driver, drops Insane Machine with an Inverted Piledriver and pins Brett Hall; still champion at the end of this range. He draws with Brett Hall by double disqualification on the Monday of Week 3, September 2007, and beats Brendan Idol with a Backdrop Driver on the Monday of Week 1, October; he is still champion at the end of this range, with Hall set to challenge him at A Haunting in America. In October 2007 he keeps the belt against Brendan Idol and Insane Machine on the Monday of Week 2 and against Brett Hall in a street fight at A Haunting in America on Saturday of Week 2; he is still champion at the end of this range, with Idol, who beats Hall by disqualification on the Monday of Week 3, set to challenge him at Pilgrimage. He keeps the belt against Brendan Idol at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, with a Backdrop Driver after Idol's springboard crossbody; he is still champion at the end of this range. He keeps the belt against Mean Jean Cattley on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 3, November 2007 in 7:41 with the Dozer Driver; in December 2007 the Mantis, a masked newcomer, steals the belt from his shoulder in the halls and challenges him for it at Winter Epiphany, and the Mantis's messenger The Trademark is knocked out by his chain-wrapped fist; he is still champion at the end of this range.

title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
label: Jim Force

won.source: The second show of the diary (Wednesday, Week 2, January 2007) bills Citizen X's win "for the USPW National title"; it does not date Force's win.

how: Jim Force's reign, which the diary does not date; it surfaces when he loses the belt to Citizen X on the second show of the diary.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Hotshots

won.source: USPW Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007 (in-game), recapped "The Hotshots defeated The Valentines to win the USPW Tag Team titles".

how: Won from The Valentines minutes after the Valentines won them, at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, with a Vessey Plex on Casey and a Fisherman's Suplex on Peter, in 1:56, when Danny Jillefski makes the pair Divinity's newest members and Seduction welcomes them; they keep the belts against The Valentines on the Monday of Week 3, with a VesseyPlex II, and are still champions at the end of this range. They keep the belts against Veteran Mentality on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 4, November 2007, when Davey Wayne pins Jim Force with the Fisherman's Suplex in 13:54, and against The Dudez!!!1!!! on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 1, December 2007 by count-out in 20:22 when Force, Oxford and Mr. Snuggleforce chase the Dudez off; the card for Winter Epiphany lists Maxmillion Productions against them; they are still champions at the end of this range.

title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
label: The Towers of Power

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Tuesday, Week 3, January 2007 (in-game), bills the match as "to win the USPW World Tag Team titles"; it does not date the Towers' win.

how: The Towers of Power's reign, which the diary does not date; it surfaces when they lose the belts to The Dudez!!!1! on the third show.
